newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada bonds open little changed in quiet trading.
newsitem.headline: Canada bonds open little changed in quiet trading.

text.p: Canadian bonds opened little changed in quiet trade on Monday, largely unaffected by weak Canadian economic data released this morning, analysts said.

"It's drifting I would say. Activity levels are moderate, as we expected with the FOMC meeting tomorrow. Even though nothing is expected out of the meeting there's always a level of uncertainty ahead of it," said Arve Bendiksrud, a fixed-income analyst with TD Securities Inc.
Canada's 30-year benchmark bond fell C$0.08 to C$119.10 to yield 6.535 percent.
The U.S. 30-year bond fell 2/32 to yield 6.54 percent. The negative spread between the bonds was one basis point, unchanged from Friday's close.
Canadian manufacturers' shipments fell 0.1 percent in June, Statistics Canada said on Monday. New orders fell 4.6 percent and unfilled orders fell 1.8 percent.

"The only possible implication you could draw from this I think is if the economy really is having a little bit of trouble, then that might have implications for how quickly the Bank (of Canada) will try to move to a neutral position," said Bendiksrud.
In other prices, Canada's 10-year benchmark bond rose C$0.05 to C$109.42 to yield 5.963 percent.
The U.S. 10-year bond rose 4/32 to yield 6.22 percent.
The negative spread between the bonds narrowed to 26 basis points from 27 basis points at Friday's close.
The 10-year Canadian government bond futures contract trading on the Montreal Exchange rose 0.25 to 120.10 with 542 contracts changing hands. A total of 3029 contracts changed hands on Friday.
